description.value: An imaging substudy of Veterans from a randomized, sham-controlled, double-blinded rTMS trial examining whether stimulation location and resting-state functional connectivity were associated with treatment response.

spans.text: An imaging substudy of 49 Veterans (mean age, 56 years; range, 27e78 years; 39 male) from a randomized, sham-controlled, double-blinded clinical trial of rTMS treatment, grouping participants by clinical response, followed by group comparisons of treatment locations identified by individualized fiducial markers on structural MRI and resting state fMRI derived networks.

value: in the active condition only, the average stimulation location of patients who respond to therapy differed from the average stimulation location of those who failed to respond

in the active condition, the fMRI time series within a subgenual cingulate region of interest would be anticorrelated with the fMRI time series within an ROI centered at the stimulation location of the responders, and not with the ROI centered at the nonresponder stimulation location
these seeds would be functionally connected with distinct brain networks

spans.text: We hypothesized that in the active condition only, the average stimulation location of patients who respond to therapy differed from the average stimulation location of those who failed to respond ( Hypothesis 1 ). Based on a mechanistic model of rTMS response [ 8 − 10 ], we further hypothesized that in the active condition, the fMRI time series within a subgenual cingulate region of interest (ROI) would be anticorrelated with the fMRI time series within an ROI centered at the stimulation location of the responders (defined as patients with > 50% change on the HAMD), and not with the ROI centered at the nonresponder stimulation location ( Hypothesis 2 ).

description.value: Randomized, sham-controlled, double-blinded clinical trial of rTMS in Veterans, with participants grouped by clinical response and treatment condition; the imaging substudy acquired structural MRI and resting-state fMRI before therapy onset for most participants or long after treatment for the remainder.

spans.text: Forty-nine Veterans with TRMD from the six centers with 3T MRIs were recruited and completed resting-state fMRI for this imaging sub-study.
